questions.question: What does a Poisson process model?
options: Sampling without replacement from a finite population
A single continuous value on a fixed interval
Random arrivals over time at a constant average rate
The median of a sample only
questions.explanation: A Poisson process models random arrivals over time at a constant average rate $\lambda$.
questions.source_support: The interpretation says it models random arrivals over time with independent arrivals and a constant average rate.
questions.polish_notes: Quality round 9: rebalanced correct-answer positions to remove option-index guessing cue

A single continuous value on a fixed interval is one random variable, not an arrival process.
The median of a sample is an order statistic, not an arrival-over-time model.

questions.question: What distribution does $N_{t+s}-N_s$ have in a Poisson process?
questions.explanation: By stationary independent increments, $N_{t+s}-N_s\sim\operatorname{Pois}(\lambda t)$ (Poisson with mean $\lambda t$).
questions.source_support: The definition states $N_{t+s}-N_s\sim\operatorname{Pois}(\lambda t)$.
